outcome_intro: Running Bitdefender GravityZone for a book of customers? Ask your AI "which customers have unmanaged or outdated machines," "what open incidents are high or critical across every client," or "which company is LAPTOP-7 in" and get one answer instead of opening each company in Control Center. The fleet commands walk your whole partner tree, so health ranking, incident triage, threat spread and monthly seat usage cover every child company.

pain_points: The GravityZone Public API is JSON-RPC, one method per call, and getCompaniesList answers one level of the company tree at a time. Every MSP script walks sub-partners and folders itself, then pages getEndpointsList per company. A Bitdefender Expert Community thread ("Powershell API - Get List of Computers") shows a hand-built paging loop that still returned the wrong group of the hierarchy.

The morning questions live on different pages: endpoint status under Network, open incidents under Incidents, quarantined files under Quarantine, seats in the monthly usage reports. Asking any of them across every customer means filtering company by company or stitching exports.

Month-end reconciliation is manual. GravityZone rolls each child company's usage up into its parent partner, so matching billed seats per customer to PSA agreements means exporting usage and working out each partner's own share by hand.

different_vs_wrappers: Integrations such as [Liongard's GravityZone inspector](https://docs.liongard.com/docs/bitdefender-gravityzone-inspector) and [Sumo Logic's GravityZone automation integration](https://www.sumologic.com/help/docs/platform-services/automation-service/app-central/integrations/bitdefender-gravityzone/) bring GravityZone data into their own platforms, and a plain API wrapper answers one JSON-RPC method for one company per call. This connector walks the whole partner tree for you, fans each question out across every child company, and saves each fleet health run as a dated local snapshot, so fleet changes, fleet locate and fleet rmm-gap can answer from it. A company it could not read completely is listed in fetch_failures, never counted as clean.
different_vs_vendor: It complements GravityZone Control Center rather than replacing it: the console stays the place for policy authoring, investigations and day-to-day response, while this skill brings cross-customer health ranking, incident triage, threat spread, machine lookup and billing reconciliation to whichever AI agent you already use.

faqs.a: Yes, on paid ChatGPT plans. ChatGPT connects to remote MCP servers over HTTPS, and bitdefender-mcp speaks HTTP natively: run `bitdefender-mcp --transport http` with BITDEFENDER_MCP_HTTP_TOKEN set (it serves `http://127.0.0.1:7777/mcp` and requires that token as a bearer header) and put that endpoint behind an HTTPS tunnel or your own reverse proxy. Step-by-step in the install guide.

faqs.q: Do I need to know how to code?
faqs.a: No. Paste one sentence into Claude Code or Codex and your agent does the install, or run a one-line installer. You enter your credentials once.

Your data stays on your machine. The CLI, the MCP server and the local snapshot store are all local. The AI sees query results, not raw bulk data, and credentials are never bundled or transmitted by MSP Skills.

faqs.q: What GravityZone API key do I need?
faqs.a: A Control Center API key: click the user icon in Control Center, choose My Account and use the Control Center API section, which also shows the Access URL. Keys are scoped per API area when you create them, with no read/write split inside an area. The fleet commands need the Companies and Network APIs, plus Licensing for usage billing, Incidents for fleet incident-queue, and Quarantine and Incidents for fleet threats. Set BITDEFENDER_API_KEY, and set BITDEFENDER_BASE_URL to your Access URL if it is not https://cloud.gravityzone.bitdefender.com/api.

faqs.q: Does it need a partner account?
faqs.a: For the cross-customer views, yes: walking child companies needs a partner-level key, because getCompaniesList is a partner API. A customer-level key works, but every fleet view then covers only that one company.

faqs.q: Will this hit GravityZone API rate limits?
faqs.a: Control Center limits each API key to a number of requests per second and answers 429 with a Retry-After header when you go over. The CLI paces itself at 5 requests per second by default (--rate-limit) and waits out a 429. getIncidentsList allows about 3 calls a minute, so fleet incident-queue makes one partner-wide call and spaces any extra pages 21 seconds apart.

faqs.q: Can the AI isolate a machine or run a command on an endpoint by itself?
faqs.a: Only if you let it. Generated commands run as soon as they are invoked and do not prompt, so preview with --dry-run first: it prints the JSON-RPC method and parameters it would send, without sending. Over MCP, the generic bitdefender_execute tool can call any GravityZone method, including isolation, kill process, remote command execution and deletes, gated only by your AI app's approval prompt. For an agent that should only read, set BITDEFENDER_MCP_READ_ONLY=1 in the MCP server's environment: bitdefender_execute then runs only GravityZone read methods, refuses every write and the reads that return or take a credential, and the import tool is hidden. Keep the approval prompt on.

faqs.q: Why does fleet changes say it has nothing to compare?
faqs.a: It diffs saved snapshots, and each fleet health run saves one (unless you pass --no-save). Run fleet health at least twice, for example daily, and fleet changes reports endpoints added or removed, managed/unmanaged flips, newly outdated agents, policies no longer applied and isolation changes between them.

faqs.q: Does it work with on-premises GravityZone?
faqs.a: It speaks the same JSON-RPC Public API, so set BITDEFENDER_BASE_URL to your Control Center's Access URL. It has not yet been verified against a live on-premises console.

faqs.q: Does it replace GravityZone Control Center?
faqs.a: No. Control Center stays best for policy authoring, investigations and day-to-day console work. This skill answers the across-every-customer questions and runs scripted actions from your AI agent.
Free. Apache-2.0 licensed. You pay only for whichever AI agent you already use.

governance_summary: The skill authenticates with a GravityZone Control Center API key you create, and its reach is exactly the API areas you enable on that key. Every fleet report (health, incident queue, threats, locate, RMM gap, changes, billing) and every list or get, except the credential reads named below, is read-only and safe to let an agent run. GravityZone is also an endpoint security console, so isolating machines, killing processes, running remote commands, scans and quarantine tasks reach real customer machines; those, plus policy, blocklist and exclusion changes, need a human to approve the exact command. Reads that return or take a credential (push settings, license keys, package settings and install links, integration settings, user password checks) are human-only. Generated commands run immediately, and the MCP server's generic execute tool can call any method, so set BITDEFENDER_MCP_READ_ONLY=1 for an agent that should only read.
